title: The Most Difficult Chinese Character
synopsis: Learn about the story behind the most difficult character in Chinese.

fullText.simplified:
Biáng biáng面，最难的汉字

    如果你问在中国的外国人喜欢吃什么？大多数人都会说：“面条”，更具体点儿就是“牛肉面”。除了牛肉面，再给大家推荐一种面——biáng biáng面，它是陕西的特色面食之一。面好吃，名字也有意思。而且biáng字还是汉字里最难写的，这个字连中国人都不会写哦！
    biáng biáng面里的“biáng biáng”是一种声音，是做面条、煮面条到吃面条，会发出的biáng biáng的声音。
    据说，biáng biáng面的“biáng”字是秦始皇发明的。当时秦始皇吃腻了山珍海味，再加上内忧外患，这些问题让他毫无食欲。这可急坏了皇宫里的人。一个太监急中生智，到街上买了碗平民小吃回来，秦始皇居然吃得津津有味，胃口大开，边吃边说：“太好吃了，简直是人间美味呀！这到底是什么呀？”太监回答：“是biáng biáng面。”
    吃完了这碗biáng biáng面以后，秦始皇马上就下令将biáng biáng面作为皇帝的专属食物。既然是皇帝专属的食物，老百姓自然就不能随便吃了。为了让biáng biáng面更加高大上，秦始皇还重新给这个面起了一个复杂的名字，连字都变得复杂得不得了。因此，biáng biáng面的“biáng”也成为了最难写的汉字。
    你如果有机会去中国陕西的话，除了去看兵马俑，一定要尝尝biáng biáng面，顺便感受一下陕西当地特有的吃面风俗。相信你会因为一碗面爱上一座城的。
fullText.traditional:
Biáng biáng麵，最難的漢字

    如果你問在中國的外國人喜歡吃什麼？大多數人都會說：“麵條”，更具體點兒就是“牛肉麵”。除了牛肉麵，再給大家推薦一種麵——biáng biáng麵，它是陝西的特色麵食之一。麵好吃，名字也有意思。而且biáng字還是漢字裡最難寫的，這個字連中國人都不會寫哦！
    biáng biáng麵裡的“biáng biáng”是一種聲音，是做麵條、煮麵條到吃麵條，會發出的biáng biáng的聲音。
    據說，biáng biáng麵的“biáng”字是秦始皇發明的。當時秦始皇吃膩了山珍海味，再加上內憂外患，這些問題讓他毫無食慾。這可急壞了皇宮裡的人。一個太監急中生智，到街上買了碗平民小吃回來，秦始皇居然吃得津津有味，胃口大開，邊吃邊說：“太好吃了，簡直是人間美味呀！這到底是什麼呀？”太監回答：“是biáng biáng麵。”
    吃完了這碗biáng biáng麵以後，秦始皇馬上就下令將biáng biáng麵作為皇帝的專屬食物。既然是皇帝專屬的食物，老百姓自然就不能隨便吃了。為了讓biáng biáng麵更加高大上，秦始皇還重新給這個麵起了一個複雜的名字，連字都變得複雜得不得了。因此，biáng biáng麵的“biáng”也成為了最難寫的漢字。
    你如果有機會去中國陝西的話，除了去看兵馬俑，一定要嘗嘗biáng biáng麵，順便感受一下陝西當地特有的吃麵風俗。相信你會因為一碗麵愛上一座城的。

raw.synopsis: Learn about the story behind the most difficult character in Chinese.
sentence_translations: Biangbiang Noodles, The Most Difficult Chinese Character
If you ask foreigners what they like to eat most in China, lots of people will say “noodles”, ..
.. or more specifically, “beef noodles”.
Apart from beef noodles, I also recommend biangbiang noodles, ..
.. one of Shaanxi Province’s specialty flour-based foods.
The noodles are very tasty, and the name is interesting too.
Biang is also the most difficult Chinese character to write. Even Chinese people don’t know how to write this character!
The “biangbiang” in biangbiang noodles represents a sound.
The “biangbiang” comes from the sound made at every stage, from making noodles, to cooking noodles and eating noodles.
It’s said that the character “biang” in “biangbiang” was created by Qin Shihuang.
At that time, Qin Shihuang was tired of eating exotic delicacies.
On top of that, the state was dealing with both internal troubles and external aggression.
All these problems caused him to completely lose his appetite.
Because of this, the people in his palace were worried sick.
One court eunuch was able to respond well under pressure.
He went out to the street and bought a bowl of commoners’ food.
Unexpectedly, Qin Shihuang ate heartily, his appetite increasing immensely.
As he was eating he said, “This is so delicious; it’s out of the world! What on earth is this?”
The eunuch replied, “It’s biangbiang noodles.”
After eating the bowl of biangbiang noodles, ..
.. Qin Shihuang immediately proclaimed biangbiang noodles to be a dish exclusive to the emperor.
Being exclusive to the emperor, common people naturally couldn’t eat it whenever they wanted.
To make biangbiang noodles even more high-end, Qin Shihuang gave them a very complicated name.
Even the characters became extremely complex.
Therefore, the “biang” in biangbiang noodles became the most difficult Chinese character to write.
If you have a chance to visit Shaanxi province, in addition to the Terracotta Army, ..
.. you must also try biangbiang noodles and experience Shaanxi’s unique noodle-eating customs.
Trust me, you will fall in love with this city over a bowl of noodles.
